blocks.title: Euler factor \(\mathrm e\)
blocks.body: We write \(\mathrm e=\exp(1)\) for the base of the natural logarithm.

blocks.title: Binary observed treatment $A$
blocks.body: We write $A\in\{0,1\}$ for the binary observed treatment, with $A=1$ denoting treated status and $A=0$ denoting untreated status.

blocks.title: Binary observed outcome $Y$
blocks.body: We say \(Y\) is the observed outcome when \(Y\in\{0,1\}\) is the binary outcome coordinate of a single observed unit drawn from the observed-data law \(P\).

blocks.title: IID observed-data model
blocks.body: The observed data are \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), where the covariate \(X\) takes values in \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), the treatment \(A\) and outcome \(Y\) are binary. For each category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) write \(p_k=P(X=k)\) for the category mass, \(\pi_k=P(A=1\mid X=k)\) for the treatment probability, and, for each treatment arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mu_{ak}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k]\) for the conditional mean outcome.

blocks.title: Fixed overlap
blocks.body:
For every category \(k\) with \(p_k>0\), the treatment probability \(\pi_k\) satisfies
\[
\epsilon \le \pi_k \le 1-\epsilon.
\]

blocks.title: Potential-outcome consistency
blocks.body:
The observed outcome agrees almost surely with the potential outcome realized under the observed treatment:
\[
Y=Y(A)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]

blocks.title: Control potential outcome $Y(0)$
blocks.body: We say \(Y(0)\) is the control potential outcome when \(Y(0)\) is a \(\{0,1\}\)-valued random variable on the same probability space as \((X,A,Y)\) whose value is the outcome under treatment level \(0\).

blocks.title: Conditional exchangeability
blocks.body:
The binary potential outcomes are conditionally independent of treatment given covariates:
\[
(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X.
\]

blocks.title: Experiment class \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
Overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\)
blocks.body:
The overlap-restricted cone of nonnegative four-cell vectors is
\[
\mathcal C_\epsilon
:=
\left\{
u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\in\mathbb R_+^4:
\epsilon(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})
\le
u_{10}+u_{11}
\le
(1-\epsilon)(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Cell functional \(\phi(u)\)
blocks.body:
For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\), with \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\) as in \cref{obj:def:overlap-cone}, define
\[
\phi(u)
=
(u_{00}+u_{01}+u_{10}+u_{11})
\left\{
\frac{u_{11}}{u_{10}+u_{11}}
-
\frac{u_{01}}{u_{00}+u_{01}}
\right\}
\]
when \(u\ne(0,0,0,0)\), and set
\[
\phi(0,0,0,0)=0.
\]

blocks.title: Average treatment effect \(\tau(P)\)
blocks.body:
For a probability law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), with arbitrary masses on this finite observation alphabet, define, for \(a,y\in\{0,1\}\) and \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), the joint cell mass
\[
q_{aky}=P(A=a,X=k,Y=y),
\]
and set
\[
q_k=(q_{0k0},q_{0k1},q_{1k0},q_{1k1}).
\]
The average treatment effect functional is
\[
\tau(P)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d}\phi(q_k).
\]

blocks.title: Minimax risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
Control outcome regression in category 1
blocks.body: We write \(\mu_{01}:=E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=1]\) whenever \(P(A=0,X=1)>0\).

blocks.title: Control outcome regression \(\mu_{02}\)
blocks.body: For an observed-data law \(P\) with \(P(A=0,X=2)>0\), define \(\mu_{02}:=E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=2]\).

blocks.title: Treated outcome regression in category 1
blocks.body: We write \(\mu_{11}\) for the conditional mean \(E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=1]\), whenever \(P(A=1,X=1)>0\).

blocks.title: Treated outcome regression in category 2
blocks.body: In the two-category witness, \(\mu_{12}\) is the treated outcome regression in the second covariate category, \(\mu_{12}=E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=2]\), and this construction sets \(\mu_{12}=0\).

blocks.title: Two-category witness law
blocks.body:
For \(d=2\) and \(0\le \epsilon\le 1\), set
\[
p_1=p_2=\frac12,\qquad
\pi_1=\epsilon,\qquad
\pi_2=1-\epsilon,\qquad
\mu_{01}=\mu_{02}=0,\qquad
\mu_{11}=1,\qquad
\mu_{12}=0.
\]
Define the corresponding full-data extension by drawing
\[
(Y(0),Y(1))=(0,\mathbf 1\{X=1\})
\]
setting \(Y=Y(A)\), and then drawing \(A\mid X=k\sim\mathsf{Bernoulli}(\pi_k)\).

blocks.title: Two-category confounding witness
blocks.body:
For every real \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\), let \(Q\) be the full-data law constructed in \cref{obj:def:two-category-witness}, and let \(P\) be its observed marginal law for \(O=(X,A,Y)\). Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Consistency.)} \(Q\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:consistency}.
\item \textbf{(Conditional exchangeability.)} \(Q\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:conditional-exchangeability}.
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\epsilon\)-overlap in the sense of \cref{obj:ass:overlap}.
\end{itemize}
The average treatment effect functional in \cref{obj:def:ate-functional} and the naive observed contrast under \(P\) obey
\[
\tau(P)=\frac12,
\qquad
E_P[Y\mid A=1]-E_P[Y\mid A=0]=\epsilon .
\]

blocks.title: ATE lower-bound transfer
blocks.body:
Fix an overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), and let \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) be the minimax mean-squared-error risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}. Then there exist constants \(a_\epsilon,b_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\) such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), if \(0<d\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and
\[
d\le b_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then
\[
a_\epsilon\left\{\frac{1}{n}+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}.
\]

cited_dependencies.locator: Theorem 2; Appendix C.5; Lemma 4; Appendix D.2
cited_dependencies.statement:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\). Let \(\mathcal D_0^{(n,d)}(\epsilon)\) be the fixed-sample binary-outcome subclass of \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) consisting of laws \(P^{\otimes n}\) with arbitrary masses \(p_k\ge0\), \(\sum_{k=1}^d p_k=1\), propensities satisfying \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass category, arbitrary treated response means \(\mu_{1k}\in[0,1]\), and \(\mu_{0k}=0\) for every \(k\). Define \(\psi_1(P)=\sum_{k=1}^d p_k\mu_{1k}\). There are constants \(a_\epsilon,b_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for all \(n\ge N_\epsilon\) and \(d\le b_\epsilon n\log n\),
\[
\inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal D_0^{(n,d)}(\epsilon)}E_P[(\widehat\psi-\psi_1(P))^2]\ge a_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\},
\]
where the infimum is over measurable estimators based on the fixed sample of size \(n\).

blocks.title: Centered endpoint estimator $\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}$
blocks.body: For \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and observed units \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), define the centered endpoint estimator by \[ \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n 2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right). \]

blocks.title: Sample law \(\mu_n\)
blocks.body: For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with single-observation law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), we write \(\mu_n=P^{\otimes n}\) for the \(n\)-fold product law of the observed sample.

blocks.title: Centered linear upper bound
blocks.body:
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\), every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\), every single-observation law \(P\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) such that \(\mu_n\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) for \(P\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:experiment-class}, define
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right).
\]
Then the mean squared error of \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) for the average treatment effect functional \(\tau(P)\) in \cref{obj:def:ate-functional} satisfies
\[
\int \bigl(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}(o_1,\ldots,o_n)-\tau(P)\bigr)^2\,d\mu_n(o_1,\ldots,o_n)
\le
\frac1n+4\left(\frac12-\epsilon\right)^2 .
\]

blocks.title: Bernoulli randomization lower bound
blocks.body:
For all positive integers \(n\) and \(d\), the minimax mean-squared-error risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, evaluated at \(\epsilon=1/2\), satisfies
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}.
\]

blocks.title: Randomized endpoint risk
blocks.body:
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(0<n\) and \(0<d\), the minimax mean-squared-error risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) defined in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies, at \(\epsilon=1/2\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac{1}{n}.
\]

blocks.title: Sample splits \(I_0,I_1\) and counts \(N^{(j)}_{aky}\)
blocks.body:
For a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), define the deterministic half-sample splits, their sizes, and the logarithmic scale
\[
I_0=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},\qquad I_1=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},\qquad m_j=|I_j|,\qquad L=\log(en),
\]
and, for each split \(j\in\{0,1\}\), treatment arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and outcome \(y\in\{0,1\}\), the split cell count
\[
N^{(j)}_{aky}=\#\{i\in I_j:(A_i,X_i,Y_i)=(a,k,y)\}.
\]

blocks.title: Chebyshev polynomial \(T_M\)
blocks.body: For \(M\in\mathbb N\), \(T_M\) denotes the degree-\(M\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind, characterized by \(T_M(\cos\theta)=\cos(M\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\).

blocks.title: Numerical cutoff $N_0$
blocks.body: We define $N_0$ to be the least $N\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every $n\ge N$, with $L=\log(en)$, $m_1=|I_1|$, $M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\}$, and $B(n)=b_0L/m_1$, the inequalities $\alpha_0L\ge2$, $4M(n)^2\le m_1$, and $4M(n)/m_1\le3B(n)/4$ all hold.

blocks.title: Falling factorial split-cell count
blocks.body: For a split-one cell count \(N^{(1)}_{aky}\) and multi-index coordinate \(r_{ay}\in\mathbb N_0\), we write \((N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}\) for the falling factorial \(N^{(1)}_{aky}(N^{(1)}_{aky}-1)\cdots(N^{(1)}_{aky}-r_{ay}+1)\) when \(r_{ay}\ge1\), with \((N^{(1)}_{aky})_0=1\).

blocks.title: Four-cell monomial $u^r$
blocks.body: For a four-cell vector \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\) and a multi-index \(r=(r_{ay})_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}\in\mathbb N_0^4\), write \(u^r=\prod_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}u_{ay}^{r_{ay}}\).

blocks.title: Calibration constant $b_0$
blocks.body: The calibration constant $b_0$ is the fixed numerical value $4096$.

blocks.title: Hybrid degree constant $\alpha_0$
blocks.body: The numerical hybrid degree constant is \(\alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{32\log 6},\frac{1}{2048\log(27/4)}\right\}\).

blocks.title: Control-cell mass $s_0(u)$
blocks.body: For a four-cell vector $u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})$, define $s_0(u)=u_{00}+u_{01}$.

blocks.title: Control outcome-one cell $t_0(u)$
blocks.body: For a four-cell vector \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), define \(t_0(u)=u_{01}\).

blocks.title: Treated outcome-one cell \(t_1(u)\)
blocks.body: For a four-cell vector \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), define \(t_1(u)=u_{11}\).

blocks.title: Degree schedule \(M(n)\)
blocks.body:
For \(n\ge2\), the logarithmic polynomial degree schedule is
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0\log(en)\rfloor\},
\]
where
\[
\alpha_0
=
\min\left\{
1,\frac{1}{32\log 6},\frac{1}{256\cdot 8\log(27/4)}
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Coefficients \(c_r\)
blocks.body:
For a nonnegative integer \(M\) and scale \(B>0\), \(c_r\) is the coefficient of \(u^r\) in the monomial expansion of the ratio-polynomial \(P_{M,B}\):
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M} c_r u^r .
\]

blocks.title: Split-size falling factorial \((m_1)_{|r|}\)
blocks.body: For the estimation-split size \(m_1\) and four-cell multi-index \(r\), the denominator \((m_1)_{|r|}\) denotes the falling factorial \(\prod_{\ell=0}^{|r|-1}(m_1-\ell)\), with the empty product equal to \(1\).

blocks.title: Light-cell approximation scale $B(n)$
blocks.body: For the calibrated hybrid estimator, the light-cell approximation scale is \(B(n)=b_0L/m_1\), with \(L=\log(en)\), \(m_1=|I_1|\), and \(b_0=4096\).

blocks.title: Factorial-moment contribution \(\widehat P_k\)
blocks.body:
For \(n\ge N_0\), set \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\). If the ratio-polynomial has monomial expansion
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r,
\]
then the factorial-moment polynomial contribution for category \(k\) is
\[
\widehat P_k
=
\sum_{|r|\le M}c_r
\frac{\prod_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}}.
\]

blocks.title: Category count \(N_k\)
blocks.body: For a sample \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i\in I\), indexed by a finite set \(I\), the category count for \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) is \(N_k=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\}\).

blocks.title: Arm-specific category count $N_{ak}$
blocks.body: For observations \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) indexed by a finite set \(I\), category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define \(N_{ak}:=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}\).

blocks.title: Hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\)
blocks.body:
Using the deterministic splits \(I_0,I_1\), split sizes \(m_j\), logarithmic scale \(L=\log(en)\), and split counts \(N^{(j)}_{aky}\) from \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}, set
\[
A_0=6,\qquad \lambda_0=256,\qquad b_0=4096,
\]
\[
D_{A_0}=8\log(9A_0/8)=8\log(27/4),
\]
and
\[
\alpha_0=\min\left\{1,\frac1{32\log A_0},\frac1{256D_{A_0}}\right\}.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), define
\[
M(n)=\max\{2,\lfloor\alpha_0L\rfloor\},\qquad B(n)=b_0L/m_1.
\]
Let \(N_0\) be the least numerical cutoff such that, for every \(n\ge N_0\),
\[
\alpha_0L\ge2,\qquad 4M(n)^2\le m_1,\qquad 4M(n)/m_1\le 3B(n)/4.
\]
For every \(n\), define the pilot-certified heavy and light category sets
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}_n
=
\left\{k:\sum_{a,y}N^{(0)}_{aky}>\lambda_0L\right\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\widehat{\mathcal H}_n^c\quad(n\ge N_0),
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}_n=\varnothing\quad(n<N_0),
\]
so that for \(n<N_0\) every category is treated by the ratio branch below. For \(n\ge N_0\), abbreviate \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\).
Put
\[
N_k^{(1)}=\sum_{a,y}N^{(1)}_{aky},
\qquad
N_{ak}^{(1)}=\sum_yN^{(1)}_{aky},
\]
and define the heavy-category ratio contribution
\[
\widehat h_k
=
\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}
\left\{
\frac{N^{(1)}_{1k1}}{N^{(1)}_{1k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{1k}>0\}
-
\frac{N^{(1)}_{0k1}}{N^{(1)}_{0k}}\mathbf1\{N^{(1)}_{0k}>0\}
\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
H_M(x)=\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2},
\qquad
E_M(x)=\frac{H_M(x)}{x},
\qquad
G_M(x)=\frac{1-E_M(x)}{x},
\]
where \(E_M\) and \(G_M\) are interpreted by polynomial continuation at zero. For \(u=(u_{00},u_{01},u_{10},u_{11})\), set
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},\qquad s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u),
\]
\[
t_1(u)=u_{11},\qquad t_0(u)=u_{01},
\]
and define the light-cell polynomial
\[
P_{M,B}(u)
=
\frac{s(u)t_1(u)}B
G_M\!\left(\frac{s_1(u)}B\right)
-
\frac{s(u)t_0(u)}B
G_M\!\left(\frac{s_0(u)}B\right).
\]
Expand
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_{|r|\le M}c_ru^r.
\]
For each category \(k\), define
\[
\widehat P_k
=
\sum_{|r|\le M}
c_r
\frac{\prod_{a,y}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}}.
\]
The heavy and light sums are
\[
\widehat T_{\mathcal H}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k,
\qquad
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
=
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\widehat P_k.
\]
The truncated balanced ratio-polynomial hybrid estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}
=
\max\{-1,\min(1,\widehat T_{\mathcal H}+\widehat T_{\mathcal L})\}.
\]
The same calibrated estimator is used for every overlap level.

blocks.title: Pilot category count
blocks.body: With the pilot-split cell counts \(N^{(0)}_{aky}\) of \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}, define the pilot category count \(N_k^{(0)}=\sum_{a,y\in\{0,1\}}N^{(0)}_{aky}\).

blocks.title: Pilot split size \(m_0\)
blocks.body: We write \(m_0:=|I_0|\) for the cardinality of the deterministic pilot split \(I_0\).

blocks.title: Pilot sandwich tail bound
blocks.body:
Let \(L=\log(en)\), and let \(m_0=|I_0|\) be the pilot-split size from \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}.  For a threshold \(t>0\), define
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}=\{k:N_k^{(0)}>tL\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}=\widehat{\mathcal H}^{c},
\qquad
B_-=\frac{tL}{2m_0},
\qquad
B_+=\frac{2tL}{m_0}.
\]
The following bounds hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Arbitrary polynomial tail.)} For every \(K>0\) and every \(c>0\), there are constants \(t_0>0\), \(C>0\), and \(N\) such that, for every \(t\ge t_0\), every \(n\ge N\), every dimension \(d\) with \(d\le c n L\), every law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and every sample law satisfying \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling},
\[
\mathbb P_{\mu_n}\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\ge B_-\}
\ \text{or}\
\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\{k:p_k\le B_+\}
\right)
\le C n^{-K}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Fixed threshold.)} For every \(c>0\), there are constants \(C>0\) and \(N\) such that, for every \(n\ge N\), every dimension \(d\) with \(d\le c n L\), every law \(P\) on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and every sample law satisfying \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}, the same sandwich event at threshold \(t=256\) obeys
\[
\mathbb P_{\mu_n}\left(
\widehat{\mathcal H}\not\subseteq\left\{k:p_k\ge \frac{256L}{2m_0}\right\}
\ \text{or}\
\widehat{\mathcal L}\not\subseteq\left\{k:p_k\le \frac{2\cdot256L}{m_0}\right\}
\right)
\le C n^{-4}.
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Combined envelope selector
blocks.body:
Fix constants \(\epsilon,C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon\in\mathbb R\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Interior overlap.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Positive constants.)} \(C_\epsilon>0\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Hybrid bound.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), if \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), then the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) of \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(0<n\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\), let \(K_\epsilon=\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}\). Define the \(C_\epsilon,\epsilon\)-dependent selected estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}\) to be \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and to be \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) otherwise. This selected estimator satisfies
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
K_\epsilon\left[
\frac1n+
\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}
\right],
\]
where \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is the minimax risk of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}.

blocks.title: Sharp fixed-interior minimax rate
blocks.body:
For an overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants \(a_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon,C_\epsilon>0\) and an integer \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that the following statements hold. Let
\[
r_{n,d}=\frac{1}{n}+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}.
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sharp sandwich.)} For every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\), and every sample law \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in \cref{obj:def:experiment-class}, if \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\), and
\[
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then the minimax mean-squared-error risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) from \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} and the hybrid estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) from \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} satisfy
\[
a_\epsilon r_{n,d}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon r_{n,d}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Parametric interior.)} For every \(K>0\), there exists \(C_K>0\) such that, for every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\), and every sample law \(P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\), if \(d>0\), \(n\ge N_\epsilon\),
\[
d\le K\sqrt n\log n,
\qquad
d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n,
\]
then
\[
\frac{a_\epsilon}{n}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\frac{C_K}{n}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Consistency threshold.)} For any sequences \(n_j,d_j\) with \(n_j\to\infty\), with \(d_j>0\) eventually, and with
\[
d_j\le \rho_\epsilon n_j\log n_j
\]
eventually, one has
\[
\mathsf R_{n_j,d_j,\epsilon}\to 0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\frac{d_j}{n_j\log n_j}\to 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

cited_dependencies.locator: Theorem 2; Appendix C.5; Lemma 4; Appendix D.2
cited_dependencies.statement:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\). Let \(\mathcal D_0^{(n,d)}(\epsilon)\) be the fixed-sample binary-outcome subclass of \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) consisting of laws \(P^{\otimes n}\) with arbitrary masses \(p_k\ge0\), \(\sum_{k=1}^d p_k=1\), propensities satisfying \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass category, arbitrary treated response means \(\mu_{1k}\in[0,1]\), and \(\mu_{0k}=0\) for every \(k\). Define \(\psi_1(P)=\sum_{k=1}^d p_k\mu_{1k}\). There are constants \(a_\epsilon,b_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon<\infty\) such that, for all \(n\ge N_\epsilon\) and \(d\le b_\epsilon n\log n\),
\[
\inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal D_0^{(n,d)}(\epsilon)}E_P[(\widehat\psi-\psi_1(P))^2]\ge a_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2n}\right\},
\]
where the infimum is over measurable estimators based on the fixed sample of size \(n\).

blocks.title: Universal hybrid envelope
blocks.body:
With \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} and \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, the following conclusions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Computability.} There is a constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) there is a finite real-arithmetic program which reads the split count vector, returns \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) exactly on every sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), and uses at most \(K d M(n)^4\) arithmetic and comparison operations.
\item \textbf{Fixed-interior calibration.} For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants \(C_\epsilon,\rho_\epsilon>0\) and \(N_\epsilon\in\mathbb N\) such that, for all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\), \(d>0\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\),
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}.
\]
For the deterministic estimator \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}\) that equals \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) when
\[
C_\epsilon\left\{\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}\right\}
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2
\]
and equals \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}\) otherwise, the same \(n,d,\epsilon\) satisfy
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\le
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P))^2\right],
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sel}}_{C_\epsilon,\epsilon}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\max\{C_\epsilon,4\}
\left[
\frac1n+
\min\left\{\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2},(1/2-\epsilon)^2\right\}
\right].
\]
\item \textbf{Centered randomization bound.} For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\) and every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\), the centered estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
2(2A_i-1)\left(Y_i-\frac12\right)
\]
satisfies
\[
\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{ctr}}-\tau(P))^2\right]
\le
\frac1n+4(1/2-\epsilon)^2.
\]
\item \textbf{Endpoint bracket.} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\) and \(d>0\),
\[
\frac{1}{100n}\le \mathsf R_{n,d,1/2}\le \frac1n.
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Calibration consequences
blocks.body:
Let \(L=\log(en)\), let \(\ell=\log n\), and let \(m_1=|I_1|\) be the second split size from \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}. Let \(M=M(n)\) and \(B=B(n)\) be the polynomial degree and light-cell approximation scale from \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Calibration cutoff.)} \(n\ge N_0\).
\item \textbf{(Large logarithmic scale.)} \(L\ge240\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
0<\ell,\qquad
\ell\le L,\qquad
L\le2\ell,\qquad
0<m_1,\qquad
n\le2m_1,\qquad
M\le L,\qquad
B\le\frac{8192L}{n},\qquad
(6^{2M})^2L^6\le n .
\]

blocks.title: Exact factorial mean
blocks.body:
Let \(d,n\in\mathbb N\), let \(P\) be a single-observation law on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and let \(k\) be a category. Suppose that \(n\ge N_0\), where \(N_0\) is the calibration cutoff in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}. With \(M=M(n)\), \(B=B(n)\), and \(\widehat P_k\) the factorial-moment polynomial estimate defined in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}, its exact mean under the iid product law generated by \(P\) is
\[
\int \widehat P_k(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\,dP^{\otimes n}
=
P_{M(n),B(n)}(q_k).
\]

blocks.title: Absolute coefficient envelope
blocks.body:
With \(P_{M,B}\), \(s(\cdot)\), \(c_r\), and \(u^r\) as in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}, write
\[
P_{M,B}(u)=\sum_r c_r u^r .
\]
For every nonnegative integer \(M\), every scale \(B>0\), and every nonnegative four-cell vector \(v\),
\[
\sum_{r\in \operatorname{supp}(P_{M,B})}|c_r|\,v^r
\le
B\,6^M
\max\left\{
\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^2,
\left(\frac{s(v)}{B}\right)^M
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Polynomial approximation certificate
blocks.body:
With the notation for \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\), \(s(u)\), \(P_{M,B}\), and \(\phi(u)\) from \cref{obj:def:overlap-cone,obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle,obj:def:cell-functional}, let \(M\), \(B\), the overlap level \(\epsilon\), and \(u\) satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(M\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Cone membership.)} \(u\in\mathcal C_\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Mass bound.)} \(s(u)\le B\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\left|P_{M,B}(u)-\phi(u)\right|\le \frac{2B}{\epsilon M^2}.
\]

blocks.title: Treatment-arm outcome count \(N_{ak1}\)
blocks.body: For a finite index set \(I\) and observations \((O_i)_{i\in I}\) with \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), we write \(N_{ak1}=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf 1\{A_i=a,\ X_i=k,\ Y_i=1\}\) for the number of observations in treatment arm \(a\), category \(k\), and outcome level one.

blocks.title: Fixed-set residual variance
blocks.body:
Let \(P\) be a law on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\), and let \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i\in I\), be an iid \(P\)-sample indexed by a finite set \(I\). Put \(m=|I|\), \(p_k=P(X=k)\), and \(\mu_{ak}=E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k]\). For a deterministic set \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
\mathcal R_a(H)
=
\sum_{k\in H}
N_k\frac{\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}>0\}}{N_{ak}}
\{N_{ak1}-\mu_{ak}N_{ak}\}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive overlap.)} The overlap level satisfies \(\epsilon>0\), and every category with positive mass satisfies
\[
\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le 1-\epsilon .
\]
\item \textbf{(Positive mass on \(H\).)} For every \(k\in H\), \(p_k>0\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
E_P\!\left[\mathcal R_a(H)^2\right]
\le
\frac{2m}{\epsilon}\sum_{k\in H}p_k .
\]

blocks.title: Finite-index product law $P^{\otimes J}$
blocks.body: For a finite index set $J$ and a probability law $P$ for one observed unit $O=(X,A,Y)$, we write $P^{\otimes J}$ for the product law on families $(O_j)_{j\in J}$ under which the coordinates are independent and each coordinate has law $P$.

blocks.title: Missing-arm second moment
blocks.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law for one observed unit \(O=(X,A,Y)\), with \(X\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and \(A,Y\in\{0,1\}\). Let \(J\) be a finite index set and write \(m=|J|\). For an iid \(P\)-sample \((O_j)_{j\in J}\), a deterministic category set \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), set
\[
Z_{ak}=N_k\mathbf 1\{N_{ak}=0\},
\qquad
N_k=\sum_{j\in J}\mathbf 1\{X_j=k\},
\qquad
N_{ak}=\sum_{j\in J}\mathbf 1\{X_j=k,A_j=a\}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(m\ge 3\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \(P\) satisfies overlap at level \(\epsilon\), the overlap parameter, and \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Mass floor.)} \(B>0\) and \(p_k=P(X=k)\ge B\) for every \(k\in H\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes J}}\left[\left(\sum_{k\in H}Z_{ak}\right)^2\right]
\le
m
+
m^2
\left[
\frac{|H|}
{\left\{((m-2)/2)\epsilon\right\}^2 B}
\right]^2 .
\]

blocks.title: Factorial product moment
blocks.body:
Fix \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and four-cell multi-indices \(r,s\). Using the split counts and split size in \cref{obj:def:sample-splits}, let
\[
\mathfrak m_{k,r}
=
\frac{\prod_{(a,y)}(N^{(1)}_{aky})_{r_{ay}}}{(m_1)_{|r|}},
\]
where \((z)_t\) denotes the falling factorial and \(|r|=\sum_{(a,y)}r_{ay}\). Let \(q_{aky}\) denote the treatment--outcome cell mass in category \(k\), as in \cref{obj:def:ate-functional}. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty estimation split.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Degree ordering.)} \(|r|\le |s|\).
\item \textbf{(Split-size condition.)} \(4|s|^2\le m_1\).
\end{itemize}
Then, under the iid product law generated by \(P\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\mathfrak m_{k,r}\mathfrak m_{k,s}\right]
\le \mathrm e\,\prod_{(a,y)}q_{aky}^{\,r_{ay}}
\prod_{(a,y)}
\left(q_{aky}+\frac{|s|}{m_1}\right)^{s_{ay}} .
\]

blocks.title: Chebyshev reciprocal coefficients \(g_{M,j}\)
blocks.body: For an integer \(M\ge2\), we say \(g_{M,j}\), \(0\le j\le M-2\), are the Chebyshev reciprocal coefficients when they are the unique real coefficients satisfying \[\frac{1-\frac{1-T_M(1-2x)}{2M^2x}}{x}=\sum_{j=0}^{M-2}g_{M,j}x^j,\] with the left-hand side interpreted by polynomial continuation at \(x=0\), where \(T_M\) is the degree-\(M\) Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind.

blocks.title: Coefficient sum certificate
blocks.body:
Let \(M\) be a positive integer and let \(z\ge 0\). With \(g_{M,j}\) denoting the coefficients of the polynomial continuation \(G_M\) in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}, define
\[
g_M^+(z):=\sum_{0\le j<M-1}|g_{M,j}|z^j .
\]
Then
\[
g_M^+(z)\le 6^M\max\{1,z^{M-2}\}.
\]

blocks.title: Heavy-cell aggregate rate
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants
\(C_\epsilon>0\) and \(\rho_\epsilon>0\), and a sample-size cutoff
\(N_\epsilon<\infty\), such that the following holds.  For every \(n,d\), every
single-observation law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and every
sample law \(\mu_n\) for \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge N_\epsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Dimension range.)} \(d\le \rho_\epsilon n\log n\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment class.)} \(\mu_n\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) for \(P\), as in
\cref{obj:def:experiment-class}.
\end{itemize}
Then the mean squared error, under \(\mu_n\), of the heavy-cell aggregate ratio branch
\(\widehat T_{\mathcal H}=\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k\) around the
pilot-heavy target \(\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\phi(q_k)\) satisfies
\[
\int
\left(
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\widehat h_k
-
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_n}\phi(q_k)
\right)^2
\,d\mu_n
\le
C_\epsilon\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Sparse factorial-polynomial mean \(\bar P_k\)
blocks.body: Given a law \(P\), a category \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), a degree \(M\), and a scale \(B\), define the sparse factorial-polynomial mean of category \(k\) by \(\bar P_k=P_{M,B}(q_k)\), where \(q_k=(q_{0k0},q_{0k1},q_{1k0},q_{1k1})\) is the four-cell mass vector for category \(k\) under \(P\).

blocks.title: Factorial-polynomial variance bound
blocks.body:
Let \(P\) be a law on the observed-data alphabet and let \(k\) be a category. With the sample splits and the calibration \(M(n)\) and \(B(n)\) defined in \cref{obj:def:sample-splits,obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}, write \(\widehat P_k\) for the factorial-moment polynomial estimate in \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle} and write \(\bar P_k\) for its sparse factorial-polynomial mean.

Assume that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty second split.)} \(m_1>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive degree and scale.)} \(M(n)>0\) and \(B(n)>0\).
\item \textbf{(Split-size calibration.)} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Light-cell mass bounds.)} The category mass \(p_k=P(X=k)\) satisfies
\[
p_k+\frac{4M(n)}{m_1}\le B(n)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
p_k\le B(n).
\]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)^2\right]
\le
8(\mathrm e+1)\left\{B(n)6^{M(n)}\right\}^2 .
\]

blocks.title: Cross-cell factorial covariance
blocks.body:
Let \(P\) be a law on the finite observed-data alphabet, and let \(k\) and \(l\) be categories.  Define \(\bar P_k\) and \(\bar P_l\) as the sparse factorial-polynomial means of the light-cell factorial estimates \(\widehat P_k\) and \(\widehat P_l\) from \cref{obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}.  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Distinct categories.)} \(k\ne l\).
\item \textbf{(Degree and scale.)} \(M(n)>0\) and \(B(n)>0\), with \(M(n)\), \(B(n)\), and \(m_1\) as in \cref{obj:def:sample-splits,obj:def:hybrid-estimator-handle}.
\item \textbf{(Split size.)} \(4M(n)^2\le m_1\).
\item \textbf{(Light-cell masses.)} \(p_k\le B(n)\) and \(p_l\le B(n)\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
  \left(\widehat P_k-\bar P_k\right)
  \left(\widehat P_l-\bar P_l\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{8M(n)^2}{m_1}\left\{B(n)6^{M(n)}\right\}^2 .
\]

blocks.title: False-light error envelope
blocks.body:
Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} For every category \(k\) with \(p_k>0\), the treatment probability satisfies
\[
\epsilon \le \pi_k \le 1-\epsilon .
\]
\item \textbf{(Calibration cutoff.)} The sample size satisfies \(n\ge N_0\), where \(N_0\) is the least numerical cutoff satisfying the calibration inequalities used in the estimator.
\item \textbf{(Logarithmic scale.)} With \(L=\log(en)\), one has \(L\ge 240\).
\end{itemize}
For the pilot-light indicator \(S_k=\mathbf 1\{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n\}\), the selected false-light error over categories whose population mass exceeds the light-cell threshold satisfies
\[
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[
\left\{
\sum_{\substack{k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\\ p_k>B(n)/4}}
S_k\bigl(\widehat P_k-\phi(q_k)\bigr)
\right\}^2
\right]
\le
8(\mathrm e+1)8192^2
\left\{
\frac1n+\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Light-cell polynomial rate
blocks.body:
Fix the overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon\le 1/2\). The following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap level.)} The fixed overlap parameter satisfies \(0<\epsilon\) and \(\epsilon\le 1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Computability.)} The hybrid estimator admits a real-arithmetic implementation: there is a universal operation-count constant \(K\in\mathbb N\), \(K>0\), such that for every \(n\) and \(d\) the program reads the split-count vector, returns \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{hyb}}\) exactly, and uses at most \(K\,d\,M(n)^4\) arithmetic and comparison operations.
\item \textbf{(Constants.)} There are constants \(C_\epsilon,c_\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Experiment and dimension.)} For every \(n,d\), every single-observation law \(P\in\mathsf{Prob}(\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}^2)\), and every sample law \(\mu_n\) satisfying \(\mu_n\in\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon}\) as in \cref{obj:def:experiment-class}, the dimension satisfies
\[
d\le c_\epsilon n\log n.
\]
\end{itemize}
Under these conditions, the light-cell contribution \(\widehat T_{\mathcal L}\) satisfies
\[
E_{\mu_n}\!\left[
\left\{
\widehat T_{\mathcal L}
-
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}_n}\phi(q_k)
\right\}^2
\right]
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\}.
\]
